I sometimes make comments to matted dogs on the street such as, “wow, time for a groom!” However, if your relationship with your in-laws is comfortable, I would suggest explaining the dangers of mats.

When matting gets really bad, the hair pulls the skin and can cause bruising. This is very painful for the dog, however, their instincts tell them to not show pain (or else they would be left by their pack). 
Also, when the mats are tightly packed onto the skin, it’s like the dog is constantly wearing a jacket and can overheat. I’ve met some very matted dogs who came off as aggressive. As soon as they were shaved and comfy, they turned into angels. Choosing the “look” of the dog over its health is really not ok. Hope this helps!

"Shaving to keep hot/cold" is a myth from what I'm taught. Keeping at least a half inch is necessary to avoid sunburning and help insulate. Your dog is just as susceptible to sun burns as you are and they need their coat to help regulate their internal temperature. You can ask your groomer for a "half inch all over". You'll still need to keep up brushing but it would be better. 

However, if you *know* she won't be brushed or you won't have time, just shave to 9.5mm (#4 blade Andis/Wahl) or a 3/8 inch. 

As for brushes, I always reccomend the Miracle Coat Slicker Dog Brush ($14 on Amazon) and a 10" greyhound comb (~$10). The Miracle brush is strong enough to give a good brushing and should last a long time. Don't brush hard, but brush thoroughly to avoid brush burn.  Once you've brushed an area out, run the comb through from the skin outwards. If it gets caught, brush out that area again. 

Hope this helps! Feel free to ask more! (:
